title.description: Event title as reported by the issuer or exchange

status.description: Event lifecycle status. `scheduled` is upcoming; `published` means the event has occurred (events flip ~2 days after their date); `cancelled` means the issuer withdrew it. List endpoints return `scheduled` + `published` and exclude `cancelled` by default. Pass the `status` query parameter to filter (e.g. `status=cancelled`).

date_precision.description: Granularity of `scheduled_at`. `exact` = timestamp known; `day` = date only; `month` = only the month is known. Consumers that need a date should still use `scheduled_at` (set to a representative point inside the window).

fiscal_period.description: Fiscal period slug (required for report-type events, e.g. `q3_2026`, `fy_2025`). For a split fiscal year the year is the one in which the fiscal year ends (2025/26 → `fy_2026`).

scheduled_at.description: Scheduled date/time in UTC (ISO 8601). For the local calendar date use `local_time` instead: a day-precision event is stored at local midnight, so its UTC instant falls on the previous day for ahead-of-UTC (Nordic) zones.

timezone.description: The issuer's IANA timezone, used to interpret `scheduled_at`. Resolved from the source article, falling back to the company's country zone.

local_time.description: `scheduled_at` rendered in the issuer's `timezone` (ISO 8601 with offset). Use this for the correct local date/time. Its date is right even for day-precision events.

scheduled_at_changed_at.description: When `scheduled_at` last changed. Useful for change-feed consumers tracking date moves.

source_article_id.description: ID of the article the event was extracted from. `null` when the article is not retrievable (not live, or removed), or when the event was first found on a company website. If a company website later supplied the date, this still names the original article, and `source` names the website. Best-effort: on the free plan it may reference an article your plan can't fetch (premium source or outside the age window).

source.description: Who published the current date. `article` is a news article or company announcement. `company_website` is the issuer's own investor relations calendar. `null` when our editors set the date.

name.description: The publisher: the outlet that carried the article, or the issuer's investor relations site. `null` when the article is no longer available.

url.description: The investor relations calendar page, for `company_website`. `null` for `article`.

article_id.description: ID of the article, for `article`. Matches `source_article_id`. `null` when the article is no longer available, and for `company_website`.

company_id.description: ID of the company this event relates to

company.description: The issuer this event belongs to, inlined so a calendar can be rendered without a lookup per row. `id` is the same value as `company_id`. `null` only when the issuer is not published by this API.

ticker.description: Primary stock ticker. `null` for an unlisted issuer.

dividend.description: Dividend lifecycle dates. `null` for non-dividend events. `scheduled_at` follows the priority ex-date > record-date > payment-date, whichever is explicitly stated.

ex_date.description: Ex-dividend date (YYYY-MM-DD). The market-event anchor: share price drops on this day.

record_date.description: Record date (YYYY-MM-DD). Holders of record on this date receive the dividend.

payment_date.description: Payment date (YYYY-MM-DD). When the cash is distributed to shareholders.

declaration_date.description: Declaration / announcement date (YYYY-MM-DD). Metadata only, never used as the calendar anchor.

kind.description: Tranche type. `ordinary` for the recurring/regular dividend; `special` for an extra/bonus/one-off dividend. When an issuer proposes both for the same date, they are returned as two separate events.

updated_at.description: When the event was last updated (ISO 8601). Use with `updated_after` for polling
